question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required'.**

(The transit of the Planet of Love happen in pairs), eight years apart every century.

options.text: The transit of the Planet of Love happens in pairs
The transits of the Planet of Love happens at pairs
The transit of Planet of Love happen in pairs

solution:
The correct answer is:** "The transit of the Planet of Love happens in pairs"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the original sentence, there is a subject-verb agreement issue.
 
• "**Transit**" is a singular subject, and the verb "**happen**" is plural, causing a grammatical error.
 
• In the sentence, the phrase "**the Planet of Love**" is the object of the preposition "**of**."
 
• The preposition "**of**" shows a relationship of possession or association between "**transit**" and "**the Planet of Love**." 
 
• In terms of subject-verb agreement, it's important to identify the true subject of the sentence to determine the correct verb form.
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**transit**." Since "transit" is a singular noun, the verb should also be in the singular form to agree with it.
 
• In this case, the singular form of the verb is "**happens**," which correctly matches with "**transit**."
 
• So, both the object of the preposition "the Planet of Love" and the subject "transit" are singular, and that's why the verb "**happens**" is used to maintain subject-verb agreement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence**: *The transit of the Planet of Love happens in pairs, eight years apart every century. *
